title: Engineer priority micro-agenda & follow-ups — 1:1 prep (Devon Park)
content:
Meeting context
- 20-minute sync, one-on-one with Devon (IC, backend infra). Keep tight: engineer prefers concrete takeaways and follow-ups.
- Primary goals: unblock roadmap ticket ENG-4521, check on on-call fatigue/health, sync on mentorship pairings.

Micro-agenda (timeboxed)
1) Quick status (3 min)
   - What shipped since last 1:1? (very short)
   - Any high-severity regressions or alerts?
2) Blockers & triage (8 min)
   - ENG-4521: pre-prod perf regression after kernel upgrade — what remains?
   - Does Devon need replicas / test environment resources?
   - Prioritization: is this urgent vs. next sprint roadmap?
3) Career / growth (5 min)
   - Pair-program rotation check (mentor match: Priya run-through?)
   - Short feedback: shipping ownership and PR reviews cadence
4) Action items & async follow-ups (4 min)
   - Confirm owners and deadlines; document in ticket; follow up in Slack channel #infra-prod.

Notes to self (manager reminders)
- Keep tone supportive — Devon flagged on-call stress in last retro. Ask one specific question about load between midnight-5am to surface fatigue patterns.
- Avoid going deep into design here; offer 1:1 follow-up pairing session if needed.
- If Devon asks for capacity, be ready to propose 2 days of focused shadowing from SRE (Avery) and a temporary test cluster.

Current status snapshot (dev-reported + my quick check)
- ENG-4521: Repro steps exist, root cause appears related to recent CUDA kernel selection change.
  - Dev repro: 3/10 runs show 2–3x latency spike at step 4.
  - Hypothesis: kernel fallback when sequence length spikes; KV cache invalidation edge case.
- PRs open: PR#1987 (serving-runtime) is in review, depends on a perf test harness change.
- CI: nightly perf job shows a 5% regression on p99 latency for 4/8 runs last week.

Questions to ask Devon (priority order)
- What do you need from me today to make progress on ENG-4521? (resource, escalation, decision)
- Is there a minimal mitigation we can ship this sprint (config toggle / graceful fallback)?
- How are you feeling about on-call bandwidth? Any specific shifts you want swapped?
- Are you still engaged with the mentor pairing? Anything I should adjust?

Proposed manager commitments (if Devon agrees)
- Approve 2 days of SRE pairing (Avery) to reproduce and harden test harness. (I can ping Avery)
- Convene a 30-min async design huddle with Priya + SRE if Devon wants design input (I will schedule).
- Add a short perf smoke to nightly job for the specific scenario causing the p99 spike; mark as priority.

Follow-ups / Action items (write into ticket & Slack in same meeting)
- DEVON: add minimal repro script to ENG-4521 and document exact timestamps for p99 spikes. (due: 2027-05-10)
- KIARA: message Avery in Slack to schedule 2-day pairing and ask SRE to reserve test cluster (due: 2027-05-07)
- KIARA: open small perf-smoke PR and link to PR#1987 (due: 2027-05-09)
- DEVON: confirm mentor session time with Priya and add short goals (due: 2027-05-13)

Risk register (quick)
- If regression persists into next week, customer-facing latency SLOs may be impacted for internal beta workloads. Contingency: automatic routing to older quantized model variant for affected customers. (needs ops runbook)

Draft Slack note to send after meeting (copy to #infra-prod):
"Quick 1:1 with Devon. Action items: pairing with SRE (Avery) to reproduce ENG-4521, PR#1987 in review, I'll open a perf-smoke PR and follow up on mentor pairing. Posting brief updates to ENG-4521. Will tag infra on-call if repro escalates. — Kiara"

Loose ideas / future discussion items (not for this meeting unless time)
- Consider opt-in post-deploy perf dashboard for teams running dedicated GPUs to catch kernel fallbacks sooner.
- Mentorship: rotate code review buddies monthly (small trial).

Quick mental note (private)
- Watch for burnout signals: declining async replies, fewer PR reviews, repeated execuses to skip pairing. If observed, propose reduced on-call for 2–4 weeks and focus on project work.

End of prep.
